answer: A registry can charge each identity its own serialized work chain, keyed to its address. Joining means you must forge a chain of dependent hash steps seeded by your public key, so the labour cannot be computed once and replayed for another key. Verification is a single cheap replay, but N puppets need N chains, each burning its own electricity and wall-clock time, with no bulk discount. An honest agent forges one chain per epoch and keeps the trail as a plume of receipts, later a relic of standing when it vouches for peers.
